subject: Forcing a coefficient to be zero conditionally

messages.author: b644a619d5622105
messages.subject: Forcing a coefficient to be zero conditionally
parts:
Hello,

I have a hierarchical model for programs, some of which are coed, some are male-only, and some are female-only. This is a variable-intercept, variable-slope model. The problem is that the coefficient of "sex" at the individual level can be modeled when the program is coed, but must be zero otherwise.

Here is my model. I put question marks on the line where I don't know what to do:

data {
  int<lower = 1> n;                       // clients
  int<lower = 1> J;                       // number of programs
  vector<lower = -256, upper = 256>[n] y; // OQ diffs
  vector<lower = 0, upper = 1>[J] RTCWT;  // RTC/WT
  vector<lower = 0, upper = 1>[n] sex;    // sex
  int prog[n];                            // programs
  real coed[J];                            // coed or not
}
parameters {
  vector<lower = -256, upper = 256>[J] a;    // intercepts
  real<lower = -256, upper = 256> g_a_int;   // program-level intercept
  real<lower = -256, upper = 256> g_a_slope; // coefficient of RTCWT
  real<lower = 0> sigma_a;                   // program-level sd
  vector<lower = -256, upper = 256>[J] b;    // slopes
  real<lower = -256, upper = 256> g_b_int;   // coefficient of sex
  real<lower = -256, upper = 256> g_b_slope; // coefficient of interaction
  real<lower = 0> sigma_b;                   // program-level sd
  real<lower = 0> sigma_y;                   // data-level sd
}
model {
  // Implicit uniform priors on g_a_int, g_a_slope, sigma_a,
  // g_b_int, g_b_slope, sigma_b,
  a ~ normal(g_a_int + g_a_slope * RTCWT, sigma_a);
  for (j in 1:J) {
    if (coed[j] == 1) {
      b[j] ~ normal(g_b_int + g_b_slope * RTCWT[j], sigma_b);
    } else {
      b = 0;  ??????????????
    }
  }
  for (i in 1:n) {
    y[i] ~ normal(a[prog[i]] + b[prog[i]] * coed[prog[i]] *sex[i], sigma_y);
  }
}

b = 0 is obviously the wrong thing to put here, but I can't figure out what works.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Forcing a coefficient to be zero conditionally

I don't understand what RTC/WT is and why you have (-256,256)
interval constraints. And why do you say the sex coefficient
can only be modeled when the program is coed?

Also, if you want conditionals, you should probably make the
data types integers. I can't tell if sex is meant to be a
binary indicator in {0, 1} or a proportion of men vs. women
in [0,1], because you declare coed[] as real and then use
it in a condition.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Forcing a coefficient to be zero conditionally
parts:
Maybe someone else will understand what you're trying to do better
than I do. I still don't understand the model or choices you're making,
but tried to answer the direct questions below.

> On Aug 19, 2015, at 7:52 PM, Sean Raleigh <sean.r...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks for following up. I wasn't sure how much detail to give about the other pieces of the model that weren't directly related to my question.
>
> RTCWT is a 0/1 indicator for the type of program. The outcome measure is a scale that is forced to be between -256 and 256.

But these are parameter declarations with names like slope and intercept.
That won't force the outcome to be between -256 and 256 --- the way to
do that is push it through a scaled tanh (or scaled and translated inverse
logit) link function.

> The coed variable is also a 0/1 indicator. (0 = not coed, 1 = coed)
>
> I tried using int declarations for these, but then I could't use them in the model. It's been a few weeks, but as I recall, multiplying things together threw errors when some of the pieces were real and some were integer.

That shouldn't happen. If you run across a reproducible case
of this, please let us know because it'd be a bug. All int
values should be promoted to real anywhere in Stan. The exception
to this general rule is arrays of ints won't get promoted to arrays
of reals, and you can't multiply arrays, only vectors and matrices.

Now where you have RWCT, you need to make that a vector to allow
multiplication, but it's not being used as a conditional indicator.
It's more efficient to do this:

if (coed[j] && RTWCT[j])
b[j] ~ normal(g_b_int + gb_slope, sigma_b);
else if (coed[j])
b[j] ~ normal(gb_int, sigma_b);
else
b[j] <- 0;

But you have to code it be careful because you can't literally do that
assignment.

> if (coed[j] == 1) {
> > b[j] ~ normal(g_b_int + g_b_slope * RTCWT[j], sigma_b);
> > } else {
> > b = 0; ??????????????
> }

if (RTWCT[j]))
b[j] ~ normal(g_b_int + g_b_slope, sigma_b);
else

> The key problem is that I want the b parameter to be modeled for the coed programs (when coed = 1) and not for programs that are single-sex (coed = 0). This makes sense because you can't compute a slope between males and females for programs that don't have both males and females.

If you really want to do this (I still don't understand what's going
on in the model), then you need to set b[j] = 0, not b = 0 (which shouldn't
even compile). But you can't assign to a parameter, so it won't work.

Instead, you need to do the more efficient thing and preprocess the
data (you can do this in transformed data) to create a vector of coefficients
just for the coed programs.

And given what you're doing, you don't want to do this b[prog[i]] * coed[prog[i]]
because you know coed[j] = 0 implies b[j] = 0, so it's just a wasted
expression evaluation and derivative calculation.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Forcing a coefficient to be zero conditionally
parts:
Just because there are no boys in girl programs or girls in boy programs doesn't mean there isn't some kind of theoretical reason to consider b_boy and b_girl for each program. You'll just get the prior as the posterior when there's no data, but if you include any other prediction model for b_boy and b_girl based on other aspects of the programs for example, you could actually figure out some small amount of evidence for a kind of hypothetical "what if we put girls in this boy only program" etc.

anyway, you could do:

y[i] ~ normal(a[prog[i]] + if_else(coed[i]==0,0,if_else(sex[i] == 1, b_boy[prog[i]], b_girl[prog[i]])), sigma_y);

or something similar.

messages.author: 37f85c6188fe5eeb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Forcing a coefficient to be zero conditionally
parts:
You don't define any actual priors over the sigmas, I assume that'd go a long way towards preventing the blow-up. Can't you at least get an order-of-magnitude guess of what sigma should be?

Also, you could break out the sigmas into sigma_b_boy, sigma_b_girl, sigma_b_coed.

or just take the empirical sigma of the posterior samples for b values for coed programs only?

All the blowup is telling you is that when you pool together the coed and the non-identifiable b values, you have a lot of variation, but the variation in the identifiable b values should be a lot smaller, hence the sigma of posterior samples for those b values should be empirically smaller.

I recommend moderately informative priors all around.
